summary.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 132 crore (+37% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 15.3 crore (+95%, margin 11.6%, +350 bps) and PAT of INR 14.8 crore (+164%). Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

segments.name: PVC additives
segments.commentary: About 70% of FY26 revenue; management said PVC sales were somewhat lower than last year, with CPVC cushioning the volatility.

segments.name: CPVC additives
segments.commentary: About 30% (around INR 110 crore) of FY26 revenue; monthly run-rate cited at INR 10-15 crore. CPVC gross margin reportedly reached 18-20%, up from 6-7% at launch two years ago.

segments.name: Oleo chemicals (Platinum Oleo Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Sales started April 2026 via contract-manufactured product; FY27 target INR 55-60 crore, with run-rate expected by Q2. Own plant to follow in roughly 1.5 years.

segments.name: Life sciences
segments.commentary: Management said it expects the life sciences division to contribute to top line in FY27 (answer to a chat question); no figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 40%; about 10% of FY27 revenue expected from Egypt, remainder from India, with most growth from CPVC and lead-free products.
FY26-29 revenue CAGR target of 35%; the 35% figure was also cited as a three-year CAGR including oleo.
EBITDA margin guided at 13-15%, which management confirmed for FY27.
Egypt plant (about 60,000 MTPA, similar capex to India) to commence production in Q3 FY27; potential revenue around INR 300 crore over three years and more than INR 600 crore at peak.
Egypt breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; Egypt output to be 50% domestic Egypt and 50% global; gross margin at least at India level and expected to be higher.
Gross margins expected to stabilise if raw material prices stabilise; some pass-through lag is expected.
capex_capacity: India capacity: Unit 2 around 60,000 tonnes and Unit 1 around 25,000 tonnes per annum (per management).
Egypt plant: about 60,000 MTPA with similar capex and facility; commercial operations expected Q3 FY27.
Palghar CPVC running at about 70-80% utilisation; remaining facility at Palghar still being installed.
Oleo chemicals: own derivatives plant planned after 1-1.5 years of pilot sales; design already started.
No capex currently planned for Europe or US manufacturing; US market under study.
demand_pricing: Management sees CPVC additives market at 50,000-1,00,000 tonnes against an estimated 50,000-55,000 tonnes currently, based on 2024 pipe production of about 2,40,000 tonnes, 85% of which used direct compound.
Customers named include Supreme Industries and Prince Pipe and Fittings; NSF-approved; now targeting smaller manufacturers.
Raw material costs rose in March on geopolitical events; company built inventory covering to end-May and says it is passing on increases, with price hikes ongoing into April.
Management said PVC prices were volatile, with a sharp spike and then fall in March-April, while chemical input costs did not follow the same pattern.
Management cited low competition in oleo chemicals and heavy R&D requirement as barriers.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 40% growth split between India and Egypt, and how much is CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% of FY27 revenue from Egypt and the rest from India; CPVC expected to grow decently, with most growth from CPVC and lead-free products.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q4 gross margin pressure come from CPVC mix, and will margins bounce back in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margins were about the same as Q3; the dip came from March raw-material price rises. Margins are expected to hold if raw materials stabilise, with a time lag in passing costs on.

qa_highlights.question: What is CPVC revenue and exit run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC revenue was about INR 110 crore of INR 450 crore in FY26; monthly run-rate ranges INR 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are CPVC gross margins versus the blended average?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC gross margin was 6-7% at launch and is now 18-20%, with management suggesting it could rise a further 2-4 percentage points as a commodity product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oleo chemicals revenue plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales started April 2026; FY27 target INR 55-60 crore, reaching run-rate by Q2; own plant to follow in about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs jump and what senior hiring occurred?
qa_highlights.answer: Employees rose from about 120 in FY25 to about 150 now and about 170 in April 2026, plus senior hires to stabilise management; employee cost to sales up about 1 percentage point, expected to normalise once the new plant runs optimally.

qa_highlights.question: What is Egypt's breakeven and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; gross margin at least at India level and higher than Indian markets; 50% domestic Egypt and 50% global sales.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility linked to crude and geopolitical events; pass-through lag could keep margins under pressure in Q1 FY27.
FY26 EBITDA and PAT grew only 4% and 4% on a consolidated basis, far below the 15% revenue growth and the FY27 40% target.
Egypt plant commissioning slated for Q3 FY27; any delay affects the 10% revenue contribution and the 35% CAGR.
Oleo chemicals revenue relies on contract manufacturing until the own plant is built in about 1.5 years; pilot sales still in progress.
Employee costs rising rapidly (120 to about 170) ahead of full utilisation of the new plant.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on FY27 targets and Egypt, but cautious on near-term gross margin, which management attributed to temporary raw-material pressure. Several answers were specific, though some (Palghar utilisation, CPVC competition) were deferred or left without numbers.
